body.text: C.0.1. oṃ namo bhagavatyai āryamahāmantrānusāriṇyai / namo vidyārājāya / namaḥ samantabuddhānāṃ //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Homage to the Blessed Noble <s>Mahāmantrānusāriṇī</s>! Homage to the King of <s>Vidyā</s>s (spells)! Homage to all the <s>Buddha</s>s!

body.text:
C.1.1.a. evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma / veṇuvane karandakanivāpe /
C.1.1.b. evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān vaiśālyṃ viharati sma / markaṭahradatīrekū ṭāgāraśālāyaṃ
C.1.2. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma / āgamayānanda yena vaiśālīti / evaṃ bhadante ty āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣīt / atha bhagavān vṛjiṣu janapadeṣu janapadacārikāñ caran vaiśālīm anuprāpto vaiśālyāṃ viharaty āmrapālīvane /
C.1.3. tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantam ānandam āmantrayate sma / gacchānanda vaiśālīṃ gatvā indrakīle pādaṃ sthāpayitvā imāni mahāmantrānusāriṇī mantrapadāni bhāṣasva / imāś ca gāthāḥ /
C.2.1. visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata /
C.2.2. buddho lokānukampaka ājñāpayati / sarvabuddhānumatena / sarvapratyekabuddhānumatena / sarvārhadānumatena (AFGH: sarvabhūtānumatena) sarvaśaikṣānumatena / sarvaśrāvakānumatena / sarvasatyavākyānumatena / pratyekabrahmānumatena / brahmānumatena / kāmeśvarānumatena / indrānumatena / devānumatena / asurendrānumatena / sarvāsurānumatena / asurapreṣyānumatena / sarvabhūtānumatena /
C.2.3. visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata /
C.2.4. buddho lokānukampaka ājñāpayati / mūmcata mūmcata mūmcata mūmcata / mā tiṣṭhantu / ītir vyupaśāmyatu / nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata /
C.2.5. buddhaḥ praviśati mahādevo devātidevo devaguruḥ sendrakāś ca devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāś catvāraś ca lokapālāḥ praviśanti anekāni ca devatāsahasrāṇy asurendrāś ca / anekāni ca asurasahasrāṇi prativasanti / bahūni ca bhūtasahasrāṇi bhagavato 'bhiprasannāni pravekṣyanti sarvasatvānām arthe /
C.2.6. te vo mānarthaṃ kariṣyanti / nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata / kṣiptaṃ palāyata / yadi yūyaṃ duṣṭacittā na palāyeta naśyeta / ye maitracittā nāparādhukāmā rakṣāṃ cānuvartayitukāmās te tiṣṭhantu mataṃ ca praviśantu /
C.2.7. buddho lokānukampaka evam ājñāpayati /
C.2.8. sumuru 4 suru 4 huru 4 mu 4 praviśati / muru 8 miri 6 muru miri 13 muru mirīti 6 ri 6 rī 6 miri 6 tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri kartā karaṃ kartā kaṃkarā karakacā / kaṃkarā 8 kaṃkaro caṃkariti kurīśe / kaṃkari 3 ṣeti / ri 6 rephasāri / phuri 7 pharā anāthānāthā siri thi phuri ruri prāsturi anāthānāthā nirgacchata ripūṃ nirgacchata yadi yūyaṃ duṣṭacittā na palāyeta naśyeta
C.2.9. buddho lokānukampaka evam ājñāpayati / praviśati sarvasatvahitādhyāśayo maitrīvihārī kāruṇiko muditāvihārī upekṣāvihārī /

children.text: C.2.10. ete mantrapadāḥ siddhāḥ siddhagāthā jinoditāḥ /
children.translated_text: These <s>mantra</s>-syllables are perfected; these perfected verses are proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One),

children.text: sarveṣāṃ devatānāṃ hi bhūtānāṃ ca hitaiṣiṇāṃ //
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all deities and beings who wish well.

body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Karandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding-ground). [Alternative:] Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Vaiśālī</s>, in the Peaked-roof Hall at <s>Markaṭahrada</s> (Monkey Pond). There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Come, <s>Ānanda</s>, to <s>Vaiśālī</s>!' 'Yes, Venerable One,' the venerable <s>Ānanda</s> assented to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One, wandering on a journey through the districts in the <s>Vṛji</s> country, arrived at <s>Vaiśālī</s> and dwelt at <s>Vaiśālī</s> in the <s>Āmrapālīvana</s> (Mango Grove of <s>Āmrapālī</s>). There the Blessed One addressed the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to <s>Vaiśālī</s>; having gone and placed [your] foot on <s>Indrakīla</s> (Indra's post), recite these <s>mantra</s>-syllables of the <s>Mahāmantrānusāriṇī</s>, and also these verses.' Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! The <s>Buddha</s>, the Compassionate One of the world, commands! By the consent of all <s>Buddha</s>s, by the consent of all <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s (solitary Buddhas), by the consent of all <s>Arhat</s>s (worthy ones), by the consent of all <s>Śaikṣa</s>s (trainees), by the consent of all <s>Śrāvaka</s>s (hearers), by the consent of all [speakers of] true words, by the consent of <s>Pratyekabrahmā</s>, by the consent of <s>Brahmā</s>, by the consent of <s>Kāmeśvara</s> (Lord of Desires), by the consent of <s>Indra</s>, by the consent of the gods, by the consent of the lord of <s>Asura</s>s, by the consent of all <s>Asura</s>s, by the consent of the servants of <s>Asura</s>s, by the consent of all beings! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! The <s>Buddha</s>, the Compassionate One of the world, commands! Release! Release! Release! Release! Let them not remain! Let the calamity be pacified! Go out! Go out! Go out! The <s>Buddha</s> enters — the Great God, the God above gods, the Teacher of gods — and the gods with <s>Indra</s>, together with <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the four World-Guardians (<s>Lokapāla</s>s) enter, and many thousands of deities, and the lords of <s>Asura</s>s, and many thousands of <s>Asura</s>s take up residence, and many thousands of beings, devoted to the Blessed One, will enter for the benefit of all beings. They will do you honor. Go out! Go out! Go out! Go out! Flee swiftly! If you, of hostile mind, do not flee, you shall perish! Those who are of friendly mind, who do not wish to do harm, and who wish to follow the protection — let them remain and enter the [Buddhist] teaching! The <s>Buddha</s>, the Compassionate One of the world, thus commands. <s>Sumuru</s> (x4) <s>suru</s> (x4) <s>huru</s> (x4) <s>mu</s> (x4) — [the Buddha] enters. <s>Muru</s> (x8) <s>miri</s> (x6) <s>muru miri</s> (x13) <s>muru mirīti</s> (x6) <s>ri</s> (x6) <s>rī</s> (x6) <s>miri</s> (x6) <s>tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri kartā karaṃ kartā kaṃkarā karakacā</s>. <s>Kaṃkarā</s> (x8) <s>kaṃkaro caṃkariti kurīśe</s>. <s>Kaṃkari</s> (x3) <s>ṣeti</s>. <s>Ri</s> (x6) <s>rephasāri</s>. <s>Phuri</s> (x7) <s>pharā anāthānāthā siri thi phuri ruri prāsturi anāthānāthā</s> — go out, enemies! Go out! If you, of hostile mind, do not flee, you shall perish! The <s>Buddha</s>, the Compassionate One of the world, thus commands. [The Buddha] enters — he whose intention is the welfare of all beings, who dwells in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), who is compassionate, who dwells in <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), who dwells in <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity).

children.text: jñānenāthottamenādya tathā dharmatayāpi ca /
children.translated_text: Through the supreme knowledge of the Lord, and also through the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: jagatām ītayaḥ sarvāḥ śāmyantv ārogyam astu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: may all the calamities of the world be pacified! May there be health for you!

children.text: C.3.1. viśaktikā yasya tṛṣṇā vidhvastā viralīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: He whose craving is poisonless, destroyed, and made sparse,

children.text: śāntacitto hy anāyāsaḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati // CDFGH: throughout: sarvaḥ svasti
children.translated_text: who is peaceful-minded and free from distress — he will bring well-being (<s>svasti</s>) to you!

children.text: C.3.2. yo jagan mokṣamārgasmin niveśayati nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the guide establishing the world upon the path of liberation,

children.text: deśakaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: the teacher of all <s>dharma</s>s — he will bring well-being to you!

children.text: C.3.3. gatir yo jagatāṃ śāstā kṛtaṃ yena sukhī bahuḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is the refuge of the world, the Teacher, by whom many have been made happy —

children.text: arthāya sarvasatvānāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all beings — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.4. yena sarvajagac caitan maitracittena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: (3.4) He by whom this entire world, with a mind of loving-kindness, the Protector,

children.text: pālitaṃ putravan nityaṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: is always guarded as [one guards] a son — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.5. gatir yaḥ sarvasatvānāṃ trāṇaṃ dvīpaḥ parāyaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: (3.5) He who is the refuge of all beings, their shelter, island, and final resort,

children.text: saṃsāre vartamānānāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: of those who are caught in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.6. yaḥ sākṣāt sarvadharmāṇām avisaṃvādakaḥ śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.6) He who directly, regarding all <s>dharmas</s> (teachings), is non-deceiving, pure,

children.text: śucivākyaḥ śucikaraḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: pure in speech and pure in action — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.7. yasmiñ jāte mahāvīre samṛddhāḥ sarvasampadaḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.7) He, the great hero, at whose birth all prosperities were fulfilled,

children.text: siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṃbhāraḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: whose aim was accomplished and whose provisions were perfected — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.8. yasmiñ jāte vasumatī savaneyaṃ prakaṃpitāḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.8) He at whose birth this earth with its forests trembled,

children.text: sarve satvāḥ pramuditāḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and all beings rejoiced — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.9. ṣaḍ vikāraṃ pracalitā yasya bodhau vasuṃdharāḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.9) He at whose awakening the earth shook with six kinds of trembling,

children.text: māraś ca durmanā āsīt sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and <s>Māra</s> became disheartened — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.10. yaśa āsīn muner yasya dharmacakre pravartite /
children.translated_text: (3.10) He, the sage, whose fame arose when the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of the Dharma) was set in motion,

children.text: āryasatyāni vadataḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: proclaiming the <s>Āryasatyas</s> (Noble Truths) — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.11. yena tīrthakarāḥ sarve jitā dharmeṇa tāyinā /
children.translated_text: (3.11) He, the Protector, by whom all the <s>tīrthakaras</s> (teachers of other paths) were conquered through the <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vaśīkṛtāḥ sarvagaṇāḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and all their assemblies were brought under control — he will bring you well-being.

children.text: C.3.12. svasti vaḥ kurutāṃ buddhaḥ svasti devāḥ saśakrakāḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.12) May the <s>Buddha</s> bring you well-being! May the gods together with <s>Śakra</s> [bring] well-being!

children.text: svasti sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvakālaṃ diśantu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May all beings grant you well-being at all times!

children.text: C.3.13. buddhapuṇyānubhāvena devatānāṃ matena ca /
children.translated_text: (3.13) By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>'s merit and by the approval of the deities,

children.text: yo yo 'rthaḥ samabhipretaḥ sarvārthodya samṛddhyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: whatever purpose is desired — may every purpose now be fulfilled!

children.text: C.3.14. svasti vo dvipade bhontu svasti vo 'stu catuṣpade /
children.translated_text: (3.14) May there be well-being for you from bipeds! May there be well-being for you from quadrupeds!

children.text: svasti vo vrajatāṃ mārge svasti pratyāgateṣu ca //
children.translated_text: Well-being for those traveling on the road, and well-being for those returning!

children.text: C.3.15. svasti rātrau svasti divā svasti madhyaṃdine sthite /
children.translated_text: (3.15) Well-being at night, well-being by day, well-being when the midday stands!

children.text: sarvatra svasti vo bhontu mā caiṣāṃ pāpam āgamat //
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you everywhere — may no evil befall them!

children.text: C.3.16. sarve satvāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarve bhūtāś ca kevalāḥ /
children.translated_text: (3.16) All beings, all living creatures, and all existences without exception —

children.text: sarve vai sukhinaḥ santu sarve santu nirāmayāḥ /
children.translated_text: may all be happy, may all be free from illness!

children.text: sarve bhadrāṇi paśyantu mā kaścit pāpam āgamat //
children.translated_text: May all see auspicious things — may no evil befall anyone!

children.text: C.3.17. yānīha bhūtāni samāgatāni sthitāni bhūmāv athavāntarīkṣe /
children.translated_text: (3.17) Whatever beings have gathered here, whether stationed on the earth or in the sky —

children.text: kurvantu maitrīṃ satataṃ prajāsu divā ca rātrau ca carantu dharmaṃ //
children.translated_text: may they always practice loving-kindness toward all creatures, and may they practice the <s>Dharma</s> by day and by night!

body.text:
C.4. ity evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān ānando bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya indrakīle pādaṃ sthāpayitvā imāni mahāmantrānusāriṇīmantrapadāni bhāṣate sma / imāś ca gāthāḥ /
C.5.1. visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata /
C.5.2. buddho lokānukampaka ājñāpayati / sarvabuddhānumatena / sarvapratyekabuddhānumatena / sarvārhadānumatena / sarvaśaikṣānumatena / sarvaśrāvakānumatena / sarvasatyavākyānumatena / pratyekabrahmānumatena / brahmānumatena / kāmeśvarānumatena / indrānumatena / devānumatena / asurendrānumatena / sarvāsurānumatena / asurapreṣyānumatena / sarvabhūtānumatena /
C.5.3. visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata /
C.5.4. buddho lokānukampaka ājñāpayati / mūmcata mūmcata mūmcata mūmcata / mā tiṣṭhantu / ītir vyupaśāmyatu / nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata /
C.5.5. buddhaḥ praviśati mahādevo devātidevo devaguruḥ sendrakāś ca devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikāś catvāraś ca lokapālāḥ praviśanti / anekāni ca devatāsahasrāṇi asurendrāś ca / anekāni cāsurasahasrāṇi praviśanti / bahūni ca bhūtasahasrāṇi bhagavato 'bhiprasannāni pravekṣyanti sarvasatvānām arthe /
C.5.6. te vo mānarthaṃ kariṣyanti / nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata nirgacchata / kṣipraṃ palāyata / yadi yūyaṃ duṣṭacittā na palāyeta naśyeta / ye maitracittā na cāparādhukāmā rakṣāṃ cānuvartayitukāmās te tiṣṭhantu mataṃ ca praviśantu /
C.5.7. buddho lokānukampa evam ājñāpayati /
C.5.8 sumuru 4 suru 4 huru 4 mu 4 praviśati / muru 8 miri 6 muru miri 13 muru mirīti 6 ri 6 rī 6 miri 6 tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri kartā karaṃ kartā kaṃkarā karakacā / kaṃkarā 8 kaṃkaro caṃkariti kurīśe / kaṃkari 3 ṣeti / ri 6 rephasāri / phuri 7 pharā anāthānāthā siri thi phuri ruri prāsturi anāthānāthā nirgacchata ripūṃ nirgacchata yadi yūyaṃ duṣṭacittā na palāyeta naśyeta
C.5.9. buddho lokānukampaka evam ājñāpayati / praviśati sarvasatvahitādhyāśayo maitrīvihārī kāruṇiko muditāvihārī upekṣāvihārī /

children.text: C.5.10. ete mantrapadāḥ siddhāh siddhagāthā jinoditāḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.5.10) These <s>mantra</s>-words are accomplished; these accomplished verses were spoken by the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) —

children.text: sarveṣāṃ devatānāṃ hi bhūtānāṃ ca hitaiṣiṇāṃ //
children.translated_text: for the welfare of all deities and beings of benevolent intention.

body.translated_text: (C.4) 'So be it, Venerable Sir!' The venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One, placing his foot upon the <s>Indrakīla</s> (threshold-post), uttered these <s>mantra</s>-words of the <s>Mahāmantrānusāriṇī</s> and these verses: (C.5.1) Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! (C.5.2) The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate to the world, commands! By the consent of all <s>Buddha</s>s, by the consent of all <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>s, by the consent of all <s>Arhat</s>s, by the consent of all learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>s), by the consent of all disciples (<s>śrāvaka</s>s), by the consent of all words of truth, by the consent of individual <s>Brahmā</s>s, by the consent of <s>Brahmā</s>, by the consent of the Lord of Desire (<s>Kāmeśvara</s>), by the consent of <s>Indra</s>, by the consent of the gods, by the consent of <s>Asura</s>-lords, by the consent of all <s>Asura</s>s, by the consent of <s>Asura</s>-servants, by the consent of all beings (<s>bhūta</s>s)! (C.5.3) Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! Disperse! (C.5.4) The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate to the world, commands! Release! Release! Release! Release! Let them not remain! Let calamity be pacified! Depart! Depart! Depart! Depart! (C.5.5) The <s>Buddha</s> enters — the great god, the god above gods, the teacher of gods — and the gods with <s>Indra</s>, and those with <s>Brahmā</s>, and those with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the four world-guardians (<s>lokapāla</s>s) enter, and many thousands of deities, and <s>Asura</s>-lords, and many thousands of <s>Asura</s>s enter, and many thousands of beings, favorably disposed toward the Blessed One, will enter — for the benefit of all sentient beings. (C.5.6) They will act for your benefit. Depart! Depart! Depart! Depart! Flee quickly! If you, of hostile intent, do not flee — perish! Those of friendly intent who do not wish to harm, who wish to follow the protection — let them remain and enter the assembly. (C.5.7) The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate to the world, thus commands. (C.5.8) <s>Sumuru</s> (×4) <s>suru</s> (×4) <s>huru</s> (×4) <s>mu</s> (×4) — he enters! <s>Muru</s> (×8) <s>miri</s> (×6) <s>muru miri</s> (×13) <s>muru mirīti</s> (×6) <s>ri</s> (×6) <s>rī</s> (×6) <s>miri</s> (×6) <s>tiri hasa miri ti mirī ri miri kartā karaṃ kartā kaṃkarā karakacā / kaṃkarā</s> (×8) <s>kaṃkaro caṃkariti kurīśe / kaṃkari</s> (×3) <s>ṣeti / ri</s> (×6) <s>rephasāri / phuri</s> (×7) <s>pharā anāthānāthā siri thi phuri ruri prāsturi anāthānāthā</s> — Depart, O enemies! Depart! If you, of hostile intent, do not flee — perish! (C.5.9) The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate to the world, thus commands. He enters — one whose intention is the welfare of all beings, who abides in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), who is compassionate (<s>kāruṇika</s>), who abides in sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), who abides in equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).

children.text: jñānenāthottamenādya tathā dharmatayāpi ca /
children.translated_text: By the supreme knowledge and likewise by the nature of <s>Dharma</s> (reality),

children.text: jagatām ītayaḥ sarvāḥ śāmyatv ārogyam astu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: may all calamities of the world be pacified! May there be health for you!

children.text: C.6.1. viśaktikā yasya tṛṣṇā vidhvastā viralīkṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.6.1) He whose thirst (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>, craving) has been detached, destroyed, and dispersed,

children.text: śāntacitto hy anāyāsaḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: whose mind is at peace, who is free from effort — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.2. yo jagan mokṣamārgasmin niveśayati nāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.6.2) He who, as guide (<s>nāyaka</s>), establishes the world on the path to liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>),

children.text: deśakaḥ sarvadharmāṇāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: the teacher of all <s>dharma</s>s — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.3. gatir yo jagatāṃ śāstā kṛtaṃ yena sukhī bahu /
children.translated_text: (C.6.3) He who is the refuge of the world, the Teacher, by whom much happiness has been made

children.text: arthāya sarvasatvānāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: for the benefit of all sentient beings — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.4. yena sarva jagac caitan maitracittena tāyinā /
children.translated_text: (C.6.4) He by whom all this world, with a mind of loving-kindness, as protector,

children.text: pālitaṃ putravan nityaṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: has been constantly guarded like a son — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.5. gatir yaḥ sarvasatvānāṃ trāṇaṃ dvīpaḥ parāyaṇam /
children.translated_text: (C.6.5) He who is the refuge of all beings, the shelter, the island, the final resort

children.text: saṃsāre varttamānānāṃ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: of those revolving in <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.6. yaḥ sākṣāt sarvadharmāṇām avisaṃvādakaḥ śuciḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.6.6) He who directly [witnesses] all <s>dharma</s>s, who is non-deceptive, pure,

children.text: śucivākyaḥ śucikaraḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: of pure speech, of pure action — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.7. yasmiñ jāte mahāvīre samṛddhāḥ sarvasampadaḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.6.7) He, the great hero, at whose birth all prosperities flourished,

children.text: siddhārthaḥ siddhasaṃbhāra sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: whose aims were fulfilled, whose provisions were perfected — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.8. yasmin jāte vasumatī savaneyaṃ prakampitā /
children.translated_text: (C.6.8) He, at whose birth this earth with its forests trembled,

children.text: sarve satvāḥ pramuditāḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and all beings rejoiced — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.9. ṣaḍ vikāraṃ pracalitā yasya bodhau vasundharā /
children.translated_text: (C.6.9) He, at whose enlightenment (<s>bodhi</s>) the earth shook with sixfold trembling,

children.text: māraś ca durmanā āsīt sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and <s>Māra</s> became disheartened — he will bring you well-being!

children.text: C.6.10. yaśa āsīn muner yasya dharmacakre pravartite /
children.translated_text: (C.6.10) He whose fame arose when the <s>Dharma</s>-wheel was set in motion,

children.text: āryasatyāni vadataḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: who proclaimed the Noble Truths (<s>Āryasatyāni</s>) — may He grant you well-being!

children.text: C.6.11. yena tīrthakarāḥ sarve jitā dharmeṇa tāyinā /
children.translated_text: (C.6.11) He by whom all the <s>Tīrthaṅkara</s>s (ford-makers) were conquered by the protective <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: vaśīkṛtāḥ sarvagaṇāḥ sa vaḥ svasti kariṣyati //
children.translated_text: and all assemblies were brought under control — may He grant you well-being!

children.text: C.6.12. svasti vaḥ kurutāṃ buddhaḥ svasti devāḥ saśakrakāḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.6.12) May the <s>Buddha</s> grant you well-being! May the gods with <s>Śakra</s> [grant you] well-being!

children.text: svasti sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarvakālaṃ diśantu vaḥ //
children.translated_text: May all beings bestow well-being upon you at all times!

children.text: C.6.13. buddhapuṇyānubhāvena devatānāṃ matena ca /
children.translated_text: (C.6.13) By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>'s merit and by the consent of the deities,

children.text: yo yo 'rthaḥ samabhipretaḥ sarvārthodya samṛddhyatāṃ /
children.translated_text: whatever aim is desired — may every aim prosper today!

children.text: C.6.14. svasti vo dvipade bhontu svasti vo 'stu catuṣpade /
children.translated_text: (C.6.14) May there be well-being for you from bipeds; may there be well-being for you from quadrupeds!

children.text: svasti vo vrajatāṃ mārge svasti pratyāgateṣu ca //
children.translated_text: May there be well-being for you going on the road, and well-being for those who have returned!

children.text: C.6.15. svasti rātrau svasti divā svasti madhyaṃdine sthite /
children.translated_text: (C.6.15) Well-being by night, well-being by day, well-being when midday stands!

children.text: sarvatra svasti vo bhontu mā caiṣāṃ pāpam āgamat //
children.translated_text: May well-being be for you everywhere — and may no evil come upon them!

children.text: C.3.16. sarve satvāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarve bhūtāś ca kevalāḥ /
children.translated_text: (C.3.16) All sentient beings, all living things, all creatures without exception —

children.text: sarve vai sukhinaḥ santu sarve santu nirāmayāḥ /
children.translated_text: may all indeed be happy; may all be free from illness!

children.text: sarve bhadrāṇi paśyantu mā kaścit pāpam āgamat //
children.translated_text: May all see auspicious things — may no one encounter evil!

children.text: C.3.17. yānīha bhūtāni samāgatāni sthitāni bhūmāv athavāntarīkṣe /
children.translated_text: (C.3.17) Whatever beings are assembled here, stationed on the earth or in the sky —

children.text: kurvantu maitrīṃ satataṃ prajāsu divā ca rātrau ca carantu dharmaṃ //
children.translated_text: may they always practice kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward [all] creatures, and may they practice <s>Dharma</s> by day and by night!

body.text:
C.7.1. iti tatra buddhānāṃ buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ devatānubhāvena mahatītir vyupaśānte ti /
C.7.2. idam avocad bhagavān āttamanās te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisatvā sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti /
C.8. (A) āryamahārakṣāmantrānusāriṇīnāmamahāyānasūtraṃ samāptam iti /
  (B) āryamahārakṣāmantrānusāriṇī samaptā /
  (C) iti mantrānusārīnīparīsamāpta /
  (E) āryamahāmantrānusāriṇīmahāvidyārajñī samāpta ti /
  (F) āryamahārakṣāmahāmantrānusāraṇīnāmamahāyānasūtraṃ rakṣākalpaṃ samāptaḥ
C.9. (A) śubham astu sarvajagatāṃ /
  (B) ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetus teṣāṃ tathāgataḥ /
  hy avadat teṣāṃ yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ / śubhaṃ /
body.translated_text:
(C.7.1) Thus there, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>s and by the power of the deities, the great calamity was quelled.
(C.7.2) This is what the Blessed One spoke, his mind satisfied. And those monks, and those <s>Bodhisattva</s>s, and that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, <s>Asura</s>s, and <s>Gandharva</s>s, rejoiced at the Blessed One's words.
(C.8) [Colophon variants:] (A) The <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Āryamahārakṣāmantrānusāriṇī</s> is completed. / (B) The <s>Āryamahārakṣāmantrānusāriṇī</s> is completed. / (C) Thus the <s>Mantrānusāriṇī</s> is fully completed. / (E) The <s>Āryamahāmantrānusāriṇī</s>, the great queen of <s>vidyā</s>s, is completed. / (F) The <s>Mahāyāna</s> <s>sūtra</s> called <s>Āryamahārakṣāmahāmantrānusāraṇī</s>, the protective ritual manual (<s>rakṣākalpa</s>), is completed.
(C.9) (A) May there be well-being for all beings in the world! / (B) Those <s>dharma</s>s that arise from causes — their cause the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared, and also their cessation: thus speaks the great ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>). Auspiciousness!
